reason: This passage (Exodus 2:11-15) is entirely narrative about Moses' actions: he witnesses an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, kills the Egyptian, flees when discovered, and seeks refuge in Midian. There is no direct speech or action from Yahweh in this text fragment, and no expression of complaint by God concerning the people. The text describes the oppression of the Hebrews by Egyptians, but this is narrative context, not God voicing complaint.
